contentBlocks.body: Good .NET test strategy starts by choosing the right feedback loop. Unit tests are fast and isolate pure rules. Integration tests prove that routing, dependency injection, authorization, EF Core mapping, and database behavior work together.
In interviews, name the behavior under test, the layer you are testing, and the tradeoff in speed versus confidence.

Pick the cheapest test that can still fail for the right reason. Pure rules get unit tests. Anything that depends on time, randomness or a third-party API gets a unit test with a fake: inject `TimeProvider` rather than calling `DateTime.UtcNow`, and fake the email provider you do not own. Anything that depends on wiring you do own (routing, DI, auth policies, EF Core mappings, the real database) needs an integration test through `WebApplicationFactory`, ideally against the same database engine you run in production. Browser journeys are the few, slow end-to-end tests at the top of the pyramid.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which behavior is best covered by an integration test?

choices: A pure method clamps a score between 0 and 100
A POST endpoint writes completion and review rows through EF Core
A simple arithmetic helper adds two values
payload.answer: A POST endpoint writes completion and review rows through EF Core
payload.explanation: That behavior crosses HTTP, auth, DI, EF Core, and persistence boundaries.

payload.text: Use unit tests for isolated business rules and ____ tests for behavior that depends on real framework wiring or persistence.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why is EF Core's InMemory provider a weak choice for integration tests?

choices: It is slower than a real database server
It cannot be used with dependency injection
It does not enforce relational constraints or translate queries to SQL, so tests can pass against behavior the real database rejects
payload.answer: It does not enforce relational constraints or translate queries to SQL, so tests can pass against behavior the real database rejects
payload.explanation: Unique indexes, foreign keys, transactions and SQL translation errors are exactly what integration tests should catch. Use SQLite or a containerized copy of your real engine instead.

payload.text: .NET 8 added the ____ abstraction so time-dependent code can be tested with a fake clock.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Plan a test suite: assign each behavior the cheapest layer that can prove it, then order the plan like a test pyramid.
